1 ⌈e-li⌉-i-ma a-na ṣú-ri-im ⌈ša⌉ šadîm(KUR) na-ap-li-ìs x [x] x x x x x
lemmas: ⌈e-li⌉-i-ma = elû III "to go up, arise; (stat.) is high"; a-na = ana I "to, for"; ṣú-ri-im = ṣūru I "cliff, rock"; ⌈ša⌉ = ša I "who(m), which; (s)he who, that which; of"; šadîm(KUR) = šadû I "mountain"; na-ap-li-ìs = palāsu I "to look (at)"
2 ši-ta-am ša i-li a-na-ku ek-mé-ku
lemmas: ši-ta-am = šittu I "sleep"; ša = ša I "who(m), which; (s)he who, that which; of"; i-li = ilu I "god, deity"; a-na-ku = anāku I "I; me"; ek-mé-ku = ekēmu I "to take away, deprive"
3 ⌈ib⌉-ri šu-tam a-ṭú-ul ki la-<ap?>-⌈ta-at⌉ ki ne-ma-⌈at ki da-al⌉-ha-at
lemmas: ⌈ib⌉-ri = ibru I "friend, colleague"; šu-tam = šuttu I "dream"; a-ṭú-ul = naṭālu I "to look"; ki = kī I "like; how?; as"; la-<ap?>-⌈ta-at⌉ = lapātu I "to touch, take hold of"; ki = kī I "like; how?; as"; ki = kī I "like; how?; as"; da-al⌉-ha-at = dalāhu I "to disturb, stir up"
4 a-⌈na⌉-ku rīmī(AM)⌈{meš} ṣé⌉-ri-im aṣ-ṣa-ab-ta-nim
lemmas: a-⌈na⌉-ku = anāku I "I; me"; rīmī(AM)⌈{meš} = rīmu I "wild bull"; ṣé⌉-ri-im = ṣēru I "back, upperside; steppe, open country"; aṣ-ṣa-ab-ta-nim = ṣabātu I "to seize, take; hold"
5 i-ša-se-šu qa-qa-ra-am i-le-te tar-bu-u’-ta-šu i-⌈ta-ki⌉-ip ša-me-e {x}
lemmas: i-ša-se-šu = šasû I "to shout, call (out); read (out)"; qa-qa-ra-am = qaqqaru I "ground, earth"; i-le-te = letû II "to split"; tar-bu-u’-ta-šu = tarbu'u I "dust (storm)"; i-⌈ta-ki⌉-ip = nakāpu I "to push, thrust"; ša-me-e = šamû I "sky, heaven"
6 i-na pa-ni-šu a-na-⌈ku? al?-tu⌉-ud
lemmas: i-na = ina I "in, on; by; from"; pa-ni-šu = pānu I "front"; a-na-⌈ku? = anāku I "I; me"; al?-tu⌉-ud = lâdu I "to bend down"
7 i-ṣa-ba-at na-x [x x x x x-i]a? la-wi-at a-hi-ia
lemmas: i-ṣa-ba-at = ṣabātu I "to seize, take; hold"; la-wi-at = lawû II "to surround; besiege"; a-hi-ia = ahu II "arm, side"
8 x-ia iš-⌈lu⌉-pa-a[n-ni x x x] x-im i-na du?-ni (x) ki x
lemmas: iš-⌈lu⌉-pa-a[n-ni = šalāpu I "to pull out, draw, unsheathe"; i-na = ina I "in, on; by; from"; du?-ni = dunnu I "power"
9 ⌈u-sú⌉-ki il-l[i]/t[u]-x [x x] x-ti-ia me-e na-di-šu [iš-q]í-a-ni
lemmas: ⌈u-sú⌉-ki = usukku I "temple, upper cheek"; me-e = mû I "water"; na-di-šu = nādu I "(water-)skin"; [iš-q]í-a-ni = šaqû III "to give to drink, irrigate"

lemmas: [i-l]um = ilu I "god, deity"; ib-ri = ibru I "friend, colleague"; ša = ša I "who(m), which; (s)he who, that which; of"; ⌈ne⌉-la-ku-šum = alāku I "to go"

lemmas: ⌈zi-mu⌉ = zīmu I "face, appearance"; ša = ša I "who(m), which; (s)he who, that which; of"; ta-mu-ru = amāru I "to see"; {d}Šamaš(UTU) = Šamaš I ""; na-am-ru-⌈um⌉ = nawru I "bright, shining"

lemmas: ša = ša I "who(m), which; (s)he who, that which; of"; me-e = mû I "water"; na-di-šu = nādu I "(water-)skin"; iš-qú-ka = šaqû III "to give to drink, irrigate"

lemmas: ìl-ka = ilu I "god, deity"; ⌈mu⌉-ka-bi-it = kabātu I "to be(come) heavy"; qa-qa-di-ka = qaqqadu I "head; capital"

lemmas: {d}Lugal-bàn-da = Lugalbanda I ""; ne-[i]n-ne-mi-id-ma = emēdu I "to lean on; impose"

lemmas: iš-ti-a-at = ištēn I "one"; ne-pé-iš = epēšu II "to do; make; build"; ši-ip-r[a]-am = šipru I "sending, mission; work"; ša = ša I "who(m), which; (s)he who, that which; of"; la = lā I "not, no; without, un-"; i-ba-aš-šu-<ú> = bašû I "to be (at hand, available); exist"; i-n[a] = ina I "in, on; by; from"; <ma>-tim = mātu I "land, country"

Translation

obv.
1 “Go up on to the mountain crag and
look at [...] ...”
2 “I have been robbed of the sleep of the gods!
3 My friend, I saw a dream:
how ominous it was, how ..., how confused!
4 I took hold of (some) bulls from the wild –
5 (one) was cleaving the ground with its bellowing,
the cloud of dust it made thrusted into the sky.
6 in front of it I leaned myself forward.
7 It seized ... [...] had enclosed my arms.
8 ... he pulled [me] forth [...] ... by force ...
9 My cheek ... [...] my ...,
[he gave] me water to drink from his waterskin.”
rev.
10 “My friend, the [god] to whom we are going,
11 is he not the wild bull, is he not very strange?
12 The countenance that you saw was shining Šamaš,
13 he will take our hand in adversity.
14 The one who gave you water to drink from his waterskin
15 was your god who honours you,
16 Lugalbanda.
We hall join forces and
17 do a thing unique,
a feat that does not (yet) exist in the land!”
